newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH BUDGET CHMN CONDITIONS HIS CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH BUDGET CHMN CONDITIONS HIS CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: Czech parliamentary deputy Jozef Wagner, one of two unaffiliated members of the lower house who may be key to whether the government wins a confidence vote, said on Tuesday his support for the cabinet was conditional.

"My voting logic is economic, not political. If the prime minister confirms my economic opinion and makes somes steps more secure for the people and the state, then if my basic demand is fulfilled, I would consider it unreasonable not to give (my vote of) confidence," Wagner told reporters outside the plenary hall as debate on the confidence vote continued.

Wagner is the chairman of the house budget committee who was expelled from the opposition Social Democrats after he voted with the government and gave Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus a narrow victory in approving the 1997 budget late last year.
Wagner said the demands which he wanted met to support the government, were about ministers' actions and "not about numbers" and that he had already discussed them with Klaus.

"(Klaus) doesn't consider (the demands) to be unfulfillable," Wagner said without elaborating on what his specific requests were. He is expected to put his demands to the government during the debate.
The ruling coalition controls 100 votes in the 200-seat house for the confidence vote which requires a simple majority of those voting for approval.

Analysts expect at least 97 opposition deputies to vote against the government, but the votes of the two unaffiliated deputies are still not clear and one deputy from the Communist party has said he is unable to vote for health reasons.

As debate began, the Communists asked that a member of parliament from the ruling coalition withdraw from voting in a show of fair play to balance the missing deputy, but a top official of one of the coalition parties told Reuters that accepting that request was "not very likely"
